description: Blocks a SUBAGENT (agent_id present) from BACKGROUNDING a long-running process: the `review` CLI, a `--watch` flag, a build/test suite (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun/deno test|build, pytest/vitest/jest/cypress/playwright, cargo/go test|build, make/rake/msbuild test|build|all, mvn/gradle test|build|verify|package), or `sleep N` with N>=10. Backgrounding = the CC Bash `run_in_background: true` flag, a standalone `&` operator (NOT `&&`; a `&` fused into `2>&1` is ignored), or `setsid`. The precise wake mechanism (agent-tools#546, reconciled with subagent-no-monitor's empirical finding): a Bash `run_in_background: true` child IS harness-tracked and DOES resume the calling subagent with its output when it exits (an ORDINARY non-labeled command backgrounded that way is allowed); a Monitor watch and a shell-DETACHED job (`&`, `nohup … &`, a `setsid` that forks — which it does, without `-w`, whenever the caller is a process-group leader) NEVER resume a subagent, and a `--watch` loop never exits, so backgrounding a labeled long process that way and ending the turn wedges the worker forever with uncommitted work and no PR (agent-tools#52). A labeled long process is blocked from backgrounding by ANY shape, `run_in_background: true` included — whether the bounded-process-under-run_in_background case should keep being blocked is a scope question tracked as a follow-up (agent-tools#559), not folded into the wording fix. The block message offers the SAME two alternatives subagent-no-monitor's does (an ordinary command under `run_in_background: true`; otherwise a bounded FOREGROUND heartbeat loop, the SYNC'd HEARTBEAT_LOOP_EXAMPLE constant). The inverse of no-long-inline-process: the orchestrator delegates long work to a backgrounded subagent; a subagent runs its OWN long work FOREGROUND and blocks. Argv-aware: a keyword inside a quoted argument to a different command never trips it. Subagent-ONLY (the orchestrator is allowed — its discipline is no-long-inline-process). Deny-by-default: no self-service bypass (ALLOW_SUBAGENT_BACKGROUND env / `# subagent-bg-ok:` sentinel removed); a would-be BLOCK consults RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_SUBAGENT_NO_BG_LONGPROC with a written justification, which asks Telegram via trusted tg-ctl and allows ONLY on an approval tap (a blank/bare 1 denies). timeout_ms 960000 covers tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus margin so a hung ask can't race the dispatcher's timeout kill into a silent on_error=open ALLOW; a CC settings entry launching cc_hook_bridge must set timeout >960s. on_error=open.
